meta.title: From shop floor to non-profit projects

goal.statement: Move from retail store management into a project coordinator role at a non-profit
goal.near_target: An offer for a project coordinator role, or a paid trial project with a non-profit
goal.marker: Running community programmes within three years

why: I'm good at running things and people; I want that to go into work I care about.
identity: I'm someone who sends the message today, not when it's perfect.

blocker.note: I worry my retail experience 'doesn't count', so I research instead of applying.

helps: A fixed slot before the kids wake
kills: Polishing one application for a week
Trackers that make me feel behind

history.why_stopped: Sent 3 applications, heard nothing, stopped trying

path.primary: Translate store-management wins into project language; apply to coordinator roles at small and mid-size non-profits
path.parallel: Volunteer to coordinate one small local project, to have something recent to point to
guardrails: Keep the current job until there's an offer
No unpaid work beyond 3 hours a week
ignored: A full master's degree for now

options_considered.reason: Closest match to what I already do
Only if interviews ask for it

lanes.name: Apply

measures.label: Message to someone in the field

starter_actions: Save one role you'd genuinely want
Message one person who coordinates projects at a non-profit

lanes.name: Proof
lanes.purpose: Recent, real evidence of project work

measures.label: Work story rewritten in project language

starter_actions: Write 3 sentences about the store refit you led
Ask the food bank if they need a coordinator for one event

ritual.trigger: After the school drop-off, before I start anything else, I open the card.
day_shape: One action from today's theme (20 minutes)
ritual.minimum_day: Save one role or send one short message
ritual.shutdown: Tap what I did; note tomorrow's first step

if_then.if: a draft is older than 2 days
if_then.then: send it as it is or delete it

if_then.if: I hear nothing back for 2 weeks
if_then.then: change the message or the target roles, not the effort
minimum day only; it still counts

checkpoints.label: Month 3
checkpoints.rethink_if: fewer than 6 weekly wins → make the plan smaller, not the goal
checkpoints.ask: Is this helping, or just tracking? Which one habit would you keep?

checkpoints.label: Month 6
checkpoints.rethink_if: 20+ applications and no interviews → retarget the roles or rewrite the CV with someone in the field

resource_floor: If shift hours change and I can't find 3 hours a week → re-plan the timeline, not the goal
surviving_habit: One message to someone in the field every week

first_action.text: Message one person who coordinates projects at a non-profit and ask for 15 minutes

compass:
WHY: my people and organising skills, in work I care about.
HOW: a card after school drop-off; one action a day from the weekday theme; count what I send, never the replies.
IF IT SLIPS: late-shift weeks are minimum days. Missing a day is normal.
PIVOT: month 3 checks the system; month 6 checks the target roles.
